Proxy returns **503 Service Unavailable** for model.safetensors, and tokenizer.json is 0 bytes. The AutoDL proxy blocks large file downloads. 

The hf-mirror.com approach is our best bet — it was progressing albeit slowly. Let me check its current progress and the ModelScope progress.

Mirror download stuck at 44M — likely stalled too. ModelScope at ~2.5MB/s progressing on ONNX files. The actual `model.safetensors` from ModelScope might download faster once it gets to it. But this is downloading way too much data.

Let me check if hf-mirror download is still running, and try a smarter approach — use ModelScope to download ONLY model.safetensors.

Mirror download still running but stalled at 44MB. Let me kill the ModelScope full download and restart it with only the files we need. Also, let me try a different strategy — use `curl` with resume capability on hf-mirror.

input.command:
nohup bash -c '
unset http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

DEST=/root/autodl-tmp/models/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct
mkdir -p "$DEST"
cd "$DEST"

BASE="https://hf-mirror.com/HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct/resolve/main"

# Download model.safetensors with curl (supports resume, better timeout handling)
echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) Starting model.safetensors download with curl..."
curl -L -C - --retry 5 --retry-delay 10 --max-time 1200 --connect-timeout 30 \
  -o model.safetensors \
  "$BASE/model.safetensors" 2>&1
echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) model.safetensors: $(stat -c%s model.safetensors 2>/dev/null || echo 0) bytes"

# Download remaining config files
for f in config.json generation_config.json preprocessor_config.json processor_config.json special_tokens_map.json tokenizer_config.json tokenizer.json vocab.json merges.txt added_tokens.json chat_template.json; do
  if [ ! -s "$f" ]; then
    echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) Downloading $f..."
    curl -L --retry 3 --max-time 120 -o "$f" "$BASE/$f" 2>&1
  fi
done

echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) All files:"
ls -lh
echo "CURL_DONE"
' > /tmp/dl_curl.log 2>&1 &
echo "CURL_PID=$!"
